📖 How to use

  1. Enter the prior probability P(D) — how common the condition is.
  2. Enter the test's sensitivity P(+|D) and specificity P(−|¬D).
  3. Press Calculate to get P(D|+) and P(D|−) with every formula step.
  4. Read the natural-frequency view (per 10,000 people) to build intuition.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is Bayes' theorem?

P(D|+) = P(+|D)·P(D) / P(+), where P(+) = P(+|D)·P(D) + P(+|¬D)·P(¬D). It updates the prior probability with the evidence from the test result.

Why can P(D|+) be low even with a 99% accurate test?

The base-rate effect: if the condition is rare, most positives come from the large healthy group, so false positives dominate. The natural-frequency table makes this visible.

What do sensitivity and specificity mean?

Sensitivity is P(positive | has condition) — the true positive rate. Specificity is P(negative | no condition) — the true negative rate.
